newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia 1996 payments balance better, still in deficit.
newsitem.headline: Zambia 1996 payments balance better, still in deficit.

text.p: Zambia's overall balance of payments improved in 1996 despite aid cuts by Western donors, but still showed a deficit of $118 million at the end of the year, finance minister Ronald Penza said on Friday.

"Preliminary estimates on the balance of payments indicate that the overall balance improved from a deficit of $261.4 million in 1995 to $118 million in 1996," Penza told parliament in his budget speech.
Penza said the improvement was due to direct private foreign investment and short-term inflows, which increased by about $41 million and $247 million respectively.
"These inflows were registered largely on account of the liberal exchange system that we have established," he said.
The current account registered a $491.4 million deficit in 1996, compared to $313.9 million in 1995.

"The rise in the current account deficit was mainly on account of increased outflows in the services account, where there was a net outflow of $208.3 million in interest payments on external debt and $235.3 million in the non-factor service payments," Penza said.
"In addition, unrequited transfers declined to $203.9 million in 1996 from $299 million in 1995," he added.
Penza said Zambia's export earnings declined by almost 18 percent to $974.9 million from $1,185.9 million in 1995 mainly because of poor copper prices.
"Earnings of copper declined to a low of $567.7 million, mainly due to a fall in prices that occurred on the international market between June and October," Penza said.
Export volumes of copper fell to 327,473 tonnes in 1996 from 341,443 in 1995.
Cobalt exports grew by 66 percent to 3,866 tonnes, increasing earnings by 42.2 percent to $192.5 million.
Earnings from non-traditional exports were estimated at $230 million.
